descriptionMarkdown:
Availability answers how difficult an item is to obtain. Provenance answers who made it, who claims it, who can 
maintain it and what happens if you are caught carrying it. A successful Requisition test never erases provenance.
Provenance Normal Access Typical Complication
Imperial General Militarum, Arbites, Inquisition, sanctioned 
institutions and ordinary Imperial markets.
Rank, paperwork, mission need, local 
shortages or questions about ownership.
Mechanicus Forge worlds, tech-priests, Skitarii supply 
and approved workshops.
Ritual restrictions, machine-cult authority, 
data access or maintenance dependency.
Kin Kin holds, guilds, prospectors and trusted 
trade contacts.
Cultural ownership, ammunition 
compatibility and reluctance to arm 
outsiders.
Provenance Normal Access Typical Complication
Aeldari Craftworld, ranger, corsair or outcast 
networks.
Imperial illegality, alien maintenance, 
hidden obligations and suspicion from both 
sides.
Proscribed / Heretical No routine lawful source.
Confiscation, corruption, Heat, 
investigation, spiritual danger or outright 
execution if exposed.
Black Market Brokers, smugglers, gangers, scavengers 
and corrupt officials.
Fraud, debt, damaged goods, traceable 
serials, betrayal or the wrong provenance.
Faction access is contextual rather than a second currency. A character normally treats equipment from their own 
institution or culture as plausible at its listed Availability. Gear from another provenance may require a contact, narrative 
permission, a +2 to +5 DC increase, or a different acquisition route altogether. Aeldari and Kin player characters do not 
automatically make their equipment legal inside the Imperium; they merely provide a believable route to obtaining and 
maintaining it.
